title: Build a zero-state task board
summary: Create, automate, and extend a small local task-board application from an empty repository.

children.title: Derive the domain architecture
children.description: Model the product domain before proposing repository structure. Identify important nouns, verbs, state transitions, invariants, cohesive units that change together, external boundaries, and dependency direction. Then map every downstream ticket, including automation, onto the smallest sound architecture. Record the approved architecture in docs/domain-architecture.md so later workers can inspect the same durable design.
acceptanceCriteria: The artifact defines a consistent domain language, behaviors, states, and invariants
Boundaries are justified by responsibilities that change together rather than technical file types
Domain logic is independent from UI, persistence, server, and automation adapters
Every downstream ticket and runtime constraint has an explicit architectural owner
docs/domain-architecture.md records the architecture for later workers
.agent-plan/verify.mjs is the repository's dependency-free verification entry point
The resulting repository structure contains no speculative abstractions

children.title: Create the runnable application skeleton
children.description: Create the minimum application shell, package scripts, and deterministic test entry point without implementing task behavior.

reviewBudget.justification: The zero-state skeleton has no narrower existing directory boundary, and these files form one runnable baseline.

acceptanceCriteria: npm start launches a page without runtime errors
npm test succeeds
The initial page has an accessible application heading and empty state
A repository-appropriate .gitignore excludes dependencies, coverage, logs, environment secrets, and OS metadata

children.title: Create and display tasks
children.description: Implement the first vertical product slice: creating valid tasks and displaying the current list. Establish the board's intentionally designed visual baseline now: use a coherent layout, hierarchy, control states, and feedback rather than browser-default presentation.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can create non-empty tasks
Empty submissions are rejected
Created tasks appear immediately
The task-creation interface has intentional, responsive visual hierarchy and states rather than browser-default styling
npm test covers the new behavior and succeeds

children.title: Run verification in GitHub Actions
children.description: Add continuous integration that uses the package scripts established by the skeleton.
acceptanceCriteria: The workflow runs for pushes and pull requests
The workflow uses Node.js 22 and npm test
The workflow grants no more than read access to repository contents
No application or package files are modified

children.title: Complete tasks
children.description: Add the active-to-completed transition while preserving task creation.
acceptanceCriteria: Active tasks can be completed
Completed state is visible and accessible
Task creation remains working
npm test covers completion and succeeds

children.title: Restore completed tasks
children.description: Add the completed-to-active transition without changing completion semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: Completed tasks can be restored to active
Completion and task creation remain working
npm test covers restoration and succeeds

children.title: Remove tasks
children.description: Add explicit task removal after completion and restoration are established.
acceptanceCriteria: Active and completed tasks can be removed
Creation, completion, and restoration remain working
npm test covers removal and succeeds

nodes.title: Persist task state
nodes.description: Store task data locally and recover safely during application startup.
acceptanceCriteria: Tasks and completion state survive a browser reload
Invalid stored data does not break startup
All previously accepted behavior remains working
npm test covers persistence recovery and succeeds
